name: Bulu (Cameroon)
notes: Bulu Latin orthography as first fixed by American Presbyterian missionaries in the 1880s (l'Alphabet de l'Église Presbytérienne du Cameroun, EPC) and described by Bates (1904), A Handbook of Bulu, with the verbal system covered by Alexandre (1966); the later PROPELCA (Programme de Recherche Opérationnelle pour l'Enseignement des Langues au Cameroun) alphabet keeps the same consonant conventions. ⟨mb⟩, ⟨nd⟩ spell single prenasalized stops /mb/ /nd/, ⟨ŋg⟩ the prenasalized velar /ŋɡ/, ⟨mv⟩ the prenasalized labiodental /ɱv/, and ⟨ngmgb⟩ the prenasalized labial-velar /ŋmɡb/ — each a single unit segment, not a nasal followed by an oral obstruent (AGENTS.md test 2, the same prenasalized-stop pattern documented for Tiv). ⟨ny⟩ is the palatal nasal /ɲ/, ⟨j⟩ the voiced palatal stop /ɟ/ (not an affricate), and ⟨ô⟩ marks the open-mid back vowel /ɔ/ as distinct from ⟨o⟩ /o/. The apostrophe marks the glottal stop /ʔ/. Smoke-tested against the Lord's Prayer opening in Bulu (Omniglot): ⟨A Tate wongan ô ne e yôb⟩ 'Our Father who art in heaven' — ⟨Tate⟩ [tate] 'Father', ⟨wongan⟩ [woŋan] 'our', ⟨ne⟩ [ne] 'is/are', ⟨yôb⟩ [jɔb] 'heaven/sky', each resolving through the mapped graphemes above. The mid-central vowel /ə/ cited in the PHOIBLE inventory has no distinct grapheme identified in the sources consulted for this pass and is left unmapped pending a citation for its spelling. Bulu is a five-tone Bantu (A70) language with no lexical word stress; tone diacritics appear in pedagogical texts but are not consistently marked in everyday orthography and are left unencoded here, a documented exemption distinct from stress (docs/quality_tiers.md).
